{{nihongo|'''Wakae Kagami Shrine'''|若江鏡神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Wakae Kagami Shrine''' (わかえかがみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Wakaeminami-chō, {{ill|Higashiōsaka|Q243863|qid=Q243863}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Main deities - Ōikazuchi Ōkami, {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}
* Associated hall deity - {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}

=== History ===
Its founding year is unknown. In the section for the fourth month of {{ill|Saikō|Q1324664|qid=Q1324664}} 1 ({{ill|854|Q24981|qid=Q24981}}) in the '{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Q1052905|qid=Q1052905}}', there is a record of advancing divine rank to "Junior Fifth Rank Lower for Ōikazuchi-Hoake-no-Myojin of {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}," thought to refer to Wakae Kagami Shrine. This shrine is also listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}', compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}).

Because {{ill|Wakae Castle|Q11616583|qid=Q11616583}} stood north of the enshrined site, it was revered by successive castle lords from {{ill|Hatakeyama Masanaga|Q5680891|qid=Q5680891}} to {{ill|Miyoshi Yoshitsugu|Q986767|qid=Q986767}}.

During the {{ill|Siege of Osaka|Q475780|qid=Q475780|lt=Osaka Campaign}} in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 20 ({{ill|1615|Q6784|qid=Q6784}}), it was struck by military fire in the {{ill|Battle of Yao (1615)|Q10892144|qid=Q10892144|lt=Battle of Wakae}} on May 6, and shrine buildings and treasures burned.

In {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 11 ({{ill|1828|Q7570|qid=Q7570}}) of the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the honden was rebuilt.

In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5) it was ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and in January {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} (Meiji 41) it was designated a shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and silk.

=== Precinct ===
* Honden (Higashiōsaka City designated {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860}}) - rebuilt in {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 11 ({{ill|1828|Q7570|qid=Q7570}}). Valuable as shrine architecture from the {{ill|Ōgosho period|Q11435433|qid=Q11435433|lt=Bunka-Bunsei era}}. It has an unusual structure with an associated hall inserted between two ikken-sha {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} halls.
* Haiden
* Shrine office
* Kagami-zuka - said to be where {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} stopped on her return from {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}} and buried a mirror.
* Distant worship site
